title: Best-of-N Sampling as an Attacker: How Many Tries to Break Safety?

original_idea.body: Best-of-N Sampling as an Attacker. Problem: measure jailbreak ASR as a function of N independent samples for open models, exposing attacker cost. Direction: draw N samples per harmful prompt, count broken if any complies usefully (StrongReject-scored), plot ASR vs N (1..64).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: cost-to-break curves give realistic robustness metrics directly relevant to deployment safety.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment: ASR vs N curve.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model, no internal access; reframes a benchmark metric.

low_compute.reasoning: N up to 64 samples per prompt; single GPU but meaningful inference budget.

novelty.reasoning: Best-of-N jailbreaking is published; ASR-vs-N curve is largely an extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Best-of-N jailbreaking is published; the attacker-effort-curve framing adds modest new angle.
